title: Email: Fw: Joel Sherman, NY Post

content.text:
From: Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>
Sent: Sunday, February 10, 2019 4:57 PM
To: Joel Sherman <joelshermn@aol.com>
Subject: Re: Joel Sherman, NY Post 
 
Hello Joel,
Hope all is well. Safe travels this spring.

This year, I don't expect them to be particularly strong anywhere. Bullpen might be OK. Going forward in the rebuild, their strength is in starting pitching potential, with guys like Mize, Matt Manning and Franklin Perez. They have solid depth behind those guys -- the farm system has gotten deeper, as a whole -- but there's still inherent risk in building around righty power pitchers.
I think their offense could be really bad. Castellanos is their best hitter and should be traded at some point; Cabrera is turning 36, coming off a significant surgery and will probably get injured again. Outside of those guys -- which isn't exactly a great 1-2 punch as is -- they're going to be counting on guys like Candelario, rookie Christin Stewart and Niko Goodrum. I don't see where the power is going to come from. It extends into the farm system, too, which is lacking in impact offensive players.

Fulmer, because if he can put together a strong first half, I'd think there will be enough suitors for a trade. His numbers were terrible last season, but his stuff was decidedly better than that. Teams seem wary of his injury history, but he's a top-of-the-rotation guy when on, and he has three years of team control remaining -- after this season. Fulmer's bounce-back is most key in the potential of a trade return: if he proves to be healthy, someone could pay up.

It looks like another uninteresting team. These guys were boring as heck last year, young, quiet and mild-mannered. I'll go with Cabrera, who brings a presence that was missing for much of last year. Cabrera, because what they need is for him to provide championship-level leadership. He has never shown such leadership, but he has never been in this position, as a veteran superstar in a clubhouse of kids on what figures to be a losing team. Given his contract, there is an odds-on chance he could lose for the rest of his career. Is he going to be cool with that? 
Cabrera is coming off the biceps surgery, Zimmermann is coming off a bunch of stuff - torn hip adductors, partially torn core muscle -- and Fulmer is coming off his third arthroscopic meniscus surgery. He's pitching with a knee brace right now. Franklin Perez missed most of last season with injuries -- they desperately need him to stay healthy this year and build up his innings count.

I don't see any of their prospects making huge impacts this season. They aren't going to rush these guys to the big leagues because they're not ready to win yet. Daz Cameron is in line to make the jump from Triple-A at some point this season, but the Tigers didn't call 25-year-old Christin Stewart up until September last season. Cameron is 22. They will be very careful with service time, as they should. Cameron has received good reviews and has enough athleticism to outperform expectations.
Has to be ownership. The Tigers have been all but rebuilding since Ilitch assumed the top spot after Mr. I died before the 2016 season. Ilitch has yet to be in a position where spending money is a priority. They will once the time is right, Avila said. How much, is yet to be determined. Ilitch profiles as more sensible with spending than his father was, perhaps significantly so - the Tigers, a mid-market team, outspending the Yankees is crazy. And though Ilitch continually says his family is committed to long-term ownership of the team, as long as Dan Gilbert exists, rumors will persist.
They brought Kaleb Cowart in on a minor-league deal and plan on having him play both ways in spring training. 
Anthony Fenech

Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: Joel Sherman <joelshermn@aol.com>
Sent: Thursday, January 31, 2019 10:29:59 AM
To: Fenech, Anthony
Subject: Joel Sherman, NY Post

Hi. Hope you have had a good offseason. Please, if this is a pain, just ignore, but I am trying to do some advance work for spring training and I was wondering if you could answer some questions about your club, please do not feel compelled to expound, any insight is appreciated:
1. What do you think is the strength of the team going forward?
2. What do you think is the weakness?
3. Do you think there is a key player?
4. Who is the most interesting person (could be player, front office, etc)/why?
5. What are the key injuries?
6. Do they have a prospect(s) who can make a difference this year?
7. Are there any wild card people/issues moving forward?
8. Is anyone doing a position change -- that could include relief to starter or vice versa, of simply a third baseman becoming a shortstop, a first baseman going to center, etc?
Thanks for any help. Rgds.
Joel
